Cemetery Hill -- July 2-3 fighting.
Cemetery Ridge -- fired canister at point-blank range into Armistead's Confederates breaching The Angle July 3. Approximately 50 yards from Armistead's men.
McPherson's Ridge July 1 -- subject of a Gettysburg Animated YouTube vignette. Hall's battery in the Railroad Cut area is precisely documented.

Devil's Den -- one of the most famous artillery positions of the battle. Guns briefly captured by Hood's Confederates then recaptured.
McGilvery's Line July 2 evening -- helped stop Confederate advance. Fought during Pickett's Charge July 3.
Long-range Parrott rifles for counterbattery fire.

Fighting withdrawal from Trostle Farm July 2 -- ordered to hold without support to buy time for McGilvery to form the Plum Run line. Lost 28 men and several guns but accomplished the mission. One of the most celebrated artillery actions of the battle.

FIRST UNION ARTILLERY TO FIRE at Gettysburg -- approximately 7:30am July 1, before any Union infantry arrived. Fought on McPherson's Ridge alongside Buford's dismounted cavalry.

commander.name: Lieutenant Alonzo Cushing
commander.fate: KIA July 3 -- killed at The Angle while serving his last gun. Received Medal of Honor posthumously 2014 -- longest gap between action and award in MOH history.

regiments.key_action: The Angle -- Cushing's battery stood directly opposite the Confederate breakthrough. As Armistead's men surged over the wall Cushing rolled his last two guns to the wall and was killed serving them.
Peach Orchard -- heavily engaged. 19 casualties.
First Corps artillery -- Seminary Ridge then Cemetery Hill.

regiments.key_action: Cemetery Ridge -- opposite The Angle during Pickett's Charge. Brown severely wounded in the cannonade.

commander.name: Lieutenant Charles Hazlett
commander.fate: KIA July 2 -- shot on Little Round Top summit beside the dying Weed

regiments.key_action: Hazlett's battery dragged its guns up the steep rocky slope of Little Round Top. Technically too elevated to fire effectively on Confederate infantry below but their moral effect was significant. Hazlett killed beside Weed -- both dying on the summit at nearly the same moment.

commander.name: Lieutenant Bayard Wilkeson
commander.fate: KIA July 1 -- both legs shattered; reportedly amputated one leg himself with a penknife before dying

regiments.key_action: Barlow's Knoll July 1 -- most exposed Union artillery position. Wilkeson had both legs shattered. He reportedly amputated one leg himself with a penknife and bled to death.

commander.name: Captain Hubert Dilger
commander.fate: Survived -- Medal of Honor for Gettysburg

regiments.key_action: Fought in the most dramatic artillery action of July 1 -- engaged Confederate infantry at close range IN THE STREETS OF GETTYSBURG to cover the Union retreat. Fighting withdrawal through the town itself.
